{
  "analysis": "The training data reveals that German legal texts frequently reference specific government bodies (Finanzamt, Magistrat, Bundesamt) and private companies (GmbH) using distinct structural patterns like 'Bescheid des [Org]', 'vom [Org]', or standalone names ending in 'GmbH'. The rules must leverage these context anchors (prepositions, case endings) to distinguish organizations from common nouns, as German capitalization alone is insufficient.",
  "strategy": "Use context-aware regex patterns anchored by legal prepositions (des, vom, durch) and specific suffixes (GmbH, AMS) to extract organization names while avoiding false positives on capitalized common nouns.",
  "note": "Every rule includes output_template and output_key. Patterns use capture groups to extract the specific entity name while ignoring surrounding context words like 'des' or 'vom'.",
  "rules": [
    {
      "name": "Tax Authority Specific",
      "description": "Matches specific named tax authorities (Finanzamt with location/number) using the 'des Finanzamtes' pattern.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "\\bdes\\s+(?:Finanzamtes\\s+(?:Wien\\s+\\d+/\\d+/\\d+|Gmunden\\s+Vöcklabruck|Innsbruck|Bruck\\s+Eisenstadt\\s+Oberwart|Vorarlberg|Österreich)|FA\\s+[A-Za-z\\s]+)\\b",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "organisation"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 5,
      "reasoning": "Captures specific named tax offices which are common in legal texts, using the genitive case 'des' as a strong anchor."
    },
    {
      "name": "General Tax Authority",
      "description": "Matches generic references to 'Finanzamt' or 'Finanzamtes' when preceded by prepositions like 'des', 'vom', 'durch', 'an das'.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:des|vom|durch|an\\s+das|von\\s+der)\\s+(?:Finanzamt(?:es)?|Finanzpolizei)\\b",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "organisation"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 6,
      "reasoning": "Extracts the organization name from the capture group while using the preceding preposition to confirm it is an entity acting in a legal capacity."
    },
    {
      "name": "City Magistrate",
      "description": "Matches Magistrates of Vienna (Magistrat/Magistrats der Stadt Wien) often followed by department numbers.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "\\b(?:Magistrat(?:es)?(?:\\s+der\\s+Stadt\\s+Wien)|Magistrats(?:\\s+der\\s+Stadt\\s+Wien)?)\\b(?:,\\s+Magistratsabteilung\\s+\\d+)?",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "organisation"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 4,
      "reasoning": "Targets the specific structure of Vienna's administrative bodies which appear frequently in parking and tax disputes."
    },
    {
      "name": "Social Security Agency",
      "description": "Matches the Federal Office for Social Affairs and Disabled Persons (Bundesamt für Soziales und Behindertenwesen).",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "\\bBundesamt(?:es)?\\s+für\\s+Soziales\\s+und\\s+Behindertenwesen\\b",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "organisation"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 3,
      "reasoning": "Matches the full official name of this specific federal agency which appears in disability and pension cases."
    },
    {
      "name": "Employment Agency AMS",
      "description": "Matches the abbreviation AMS (Arbeitsmarktservice) when used as an organization.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "\\bAMS\\b",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "organisation"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 2,
      "reasoning": "Simple acronym match for the employment agency, which is a distinct entity type in these texts."
    },
    {
      "name": "Private Companies GmbH",
      "description": "Matches private companies ending in GmbH, often preceded by 'der' or 'der ... GmbH'.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "\\b[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]+)*\\s+GmbH\\b",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "organisation"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 7,
      "reasoning": "Captures private limited liability companies. The pattern requires the 'GmbH' suffix to avoid matching generic capitalized nouns."
    },
    {
      "name": "Fraud Investigation Office",
      "description": "Matches the Amt für Betrugsbekämpfung.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "\\bAmt\\s+für\\s+Betrugsbekämpfung\\b",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "organisation"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 2,
      "reasoning": "Specific match for the fraud investigation office mentioned in the training data."
    }
  ],
  "deleted_rules": []
}

- USE CONTEXT: The same string can mean different things. Match surrounding words/punctuation and use capture groups ($1) to extract just the value.
- ONE RULE, ONE PATTERN: Multiple focused rules beat one giant regex. Each rule should have a clear, testable reason to exist.

WHAT MAKES A GOOD RULE:
- PRECISION OVER RECALL: A rule that matches 10 things correctly beats one that matches 100 with 20 wrong. Never sacrifice precision for recall. Missing a match is fixable later; a wrong match poisons results.
- GENERALIZE, DON'T MEMORIZE: Rules run on unseen text. Match the *structure* of values, not the exact strings you see in training data.
- USE CONTEXT: The same string can mean different things. Match surrounding words/punctuation and use capture groups ($1) to extract just the value.
- ONE RULE, ONE PATTERN: Multiple focused rules beat one giant regex. Each rule should have a clear, testable reason to exist.

GOOD vs BAD PATTERNS (learn from these):
